title: Classic terminal, screen-reader, TUI, and JSON projections
objective: Project one semantic decision consistently across interactive TUI, classic terminal, append-only screen reader, and machine-readable JSON while preserving each surface's protocol.
requirements: TUI D1/D2/D3 renders semantic summary, structured detail, and safe full evidence.
Classic and screen-reader surfaces share semantic tool presentation and terminal group summaries.
Screen-reader output is append-only, textual, bounded, control-character safe, and free of spinner/tick noise.
JSON emits every raw call/result event and bypasses visual aggregation.

acceptance.criterion: Classic and screen-reader output use semantic summaries and never hide failures.
Registered screen-reader commands and aliases never fall through to unknown, and mirrored command bodies render once.
Routine events group visually while JSON keeps every call, result, and structured SendUserMessage content block.
Narrow layouts retain textual state and decisions without relying on color or animation.
Dynamic resize preserves emoji, ZWJ, combining marks, ambiguous-width text, and input state.
Adapter-owned aggregate, action, terminal, and screen-reader copy follows the active runtime language with complete six-language semantic keys.

commands.command: tmux pane: go test ./tui -run decision/root viewport matrix

remaining_risks: IDE terminal and real assistive-technology certification require host-specific manual testing.

result.summary: All interactive projections share semantics; JSON remains lossless and screen-reader output remains linear.
